digest.component_or_area: Jira inbound reconciliation (fetcher, differ, field application)
propositions: When a parent is removed in Jira, the fetcher omits the absent parent from the snapshot instead of explicitly recording it as None, making the de-parenting invisible to downstream layers.

The inbound differ refuses to emit parent_id=None to avoid spurious clears on unresolved parent keys, but this collapses two distinct cases (observed-absent vs. not-yet-resolved) into one, preventing legitimate clear mutations.

A parent clear must be emitted only when positive evidence exists that Jira was queried and answered no parent, distinguished from read failures or unresolvable keys via three-state classification (unobserved, no-parent, resolved, unresolvable).
The apply layer is already capable of handling parent_id=None by mapping it to empty string, so the defect is purely in detection and emission, not in application.

An unmanaged parent (one rebar never set locally) must not be cleared inbound even if Jira has no parent, to avoid clobbering local state; the same-pass outbound-write suppression gates the clear as an additional safeguard.

The snapshot schema and integration tests must be updated to distinguish authoritative-parentless (key present, value None) from never-queried (key absent), following the same pattern already established for issuelinks.
